question.text: Neelgiri AIF has 55% of its corpus contributed by LPs whose beneficial owners are citizens of China. Under SEBI's Oct 8, 2024 circular on Specific Due Diligence (referencing Rule 6 of FEMA NDI Rules), when must the AIF report its investments to the Custodian?

answer.text: No reporting is required if the investors are passive LPs

Specific DD must be conducted before making any investment; any investment where the scheme holds ≥10% of equity/equity-linked securities of an investee (fully diluted) must be reported to Custodian within 30 days of investment

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI Circular dated Oct 8, 2024 requires specific DD (per SFA implementation standards) by an AIF scheme where 50%+ of corpus is contributed by investors (or their beneficial owners) who are citizens/residents of land-border-sharing countries (China, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar) under Rule 6 of NDI Rules. Upon DD, if the AIF holds ≥10% of equity/equity-linked securities (fully diluted) in any investee, the scheme must REPORT to its Custodian within 30 DAYS of investment in the SFA-specified format. Existing investments crossing the 10% threshold must also be reported within prescribed timeline. The Trap: Option A defers reporting to annual audit (too late). Option B ignores active-DD obligations. Option C is reactive; proactive DD is mandated. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers specific DD frameworks (QIB, QB, RBI-evergreening, land-border — all four from SEBI Oct 2024 circular). Under Rule 6(a) NDI, land-border country investors require Government approval route for direct equity. AIF route doesn't circumvent this. Manager's Pro-Tip: Maintain LP-side BO 'land-border flag' at onboarding. If the 50% threshold is crossed mid-tenure (e.g., by LP transfers), trigger fresh DD before the next investment. Custodian agreements should have specific reporting templates and 30-day SLA built in.
